clue.text: Time after parties when a certain amount of drug is on offer

indicators.note: after places the time word behind the parties word in the answer

parts.note: dos are parties or celebrations, as in an office do
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Late in the evening, once the parties are over, someone is dealing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose measured out for a patient is a specified quantity of medicine.

clue.text: Fathers carrying big gun? Horrible types

indicators.note: carrying means the fathers word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: dads is an informal word for fathers
a big gun is an important person, a star

explanation.surface: Gun-toting fathers are described as horrible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big gun' looks like a weapon the fathers carry, but it is slang for a leading figure; 'carrying' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastards is an old word for cowardly, despicable villains.

clue.text: Wound allowed to get red

parts.note: a scar is the mark of a healed wound
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: An injury left alone turns red and inflamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid shade of red.

clue.text: One bird or another protecting egg that's very big

indicators.note: protecting means the second bird wraps around the other letters

parts.note: another bird here is a gander, a male goose
an egg is round like the letter O
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: One bird, or perhaps another, guards an enormous egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bird or another' looks like a single vague phrase, but 'One bird' is the definition and 'another' is the gander. OS, short for outsize, is a clothing-label size.
explanation.definitionFit: A goosander is a kind of diving duck, a sawbill.

clue.text: Birds splash around in far side of ness

indicators.note: in places the splashing word inside the letters taken from the end of ness

parts.note: the far side of the word ness is its final pair of letters
to wallow is to splash around in water or mud

explanation.surface: Birds are seen paddling about on the distant shore of a Scottish headland.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a Scottish headland, which suits the birds, but only the word's closing pair of letters is used, with 'in' placing the splashing word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows are small fork-tailed migratory songbirds.

clue.text: Water in east, hot otherwise? It might give you that

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in a different way, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rain in the east and heat elsewhere: something reports such conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges WATER IN EAST HOT; 'that' points back to the weather the first part describes, wet in one region and hot in another.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological station measures and reports rain and temperature, the kind of conditions described.

clue.text: Like non-fattening food in pub

explanation.surface: Diet meals served at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LO-CAL it is shorthand for low-calorie; the whole word is the British name for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-cal describes low-calorie dishes, and a local is the neighbourhood tavern one regularly drinks in.

clue.text: Like certain goods brought by donor — derisory

indicators.note: brought by means the letters are carried within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A donor offers some goods, but the gift is pitiful.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the dash, from the end of 'donor' into the start of 'derisory'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on order have been requested from a supplier but not yet delivered.

clue.text: After first sign of sun asks for showers

indicators.note: After places the asking word behind the letter from sun
first sign of picks out the opening letter of the word sun

parts.note: prays can mean asks earnestly, as in 'pray tell'

explanation.surface: Someone sees the sun and then begs for rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link; PRAYS on its own means asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprays are fine showers of liquid droplets.

clue.text: Big-timers do not fancy being put in a small flat

indicators.note: fancy here is an adjective meaning elaborate or reworked, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wealthy high-fliers dislike being housed in a tiny apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do not fancy' reads as dislike, but 'do not' is part of the fodder and 'fancy' alone rearranges BIG-TIMERS DO NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsitting room is a single rented room used for both living and sleeping, a bedsit.

clue.text: So a poet and artist appear together in TV series?

parts.note: Alexander Pope was an English poet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A poet and a painter team up on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Alexander Pope; RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running television drama serial.

clue.text: Church gets nothing right — admission of one group within it?

indicators.note: admission of means the numeral is let in between the other letters

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A church comes up empty-handed when someone admits to belonging to a clique within it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the church: the definition reads the group as one that is part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a body of singers belonging to a church congregation.

clue.text: A t-tragic king's listening intently

parts.note: the stutter in t-tragic tells you to stammer the king's name too: Lear, Shakespeare's tragic king, becomes L-LEAR, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A stammering account of a tragic monarch's grief holds the audience rapt.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 't-tragic' signals that the king, Shakespeare's King Lear, should be stammered as well, doubling his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is an idiom for paying full attention.

clue.text: Princess in very good break from work

indicators.note: in places the princess inside the word for very good

parts.note: holy describes someone saintly, very good
Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: A royal enjoys a virtuous rest from her duties.
explanation.walkthrough: IDA is Princess Ida, title character of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a vacation, time off from one's job.

clue.text: Notice returning fifties rocker being old-fashioned

indicators.note: returning means the notice word comes back to front

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth who followed rock and roll

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about an ageing rock fan coming back looks behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys, Teds for short, were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated has gone out of style.

clue.text: Dogs make mistake getting into rows

indicators.note: getting into means the error word goes inside the rows word

parts.note: tiers are rows stacked one above another
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Dogs blunder in among lines of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Terriers are a family of small, energetic hunting breeds.

clue.text: Fashionable archdeacon is on Conservative list

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A trendy senior cleric appears on the Tory party's roster.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete catalogue of goods or items.

clue.text: Journalist gets very important lady upset, having left her

annotationWithheld.why: Journalist gets very important lady upset, having left her (8): REPORTER as held; no reading of 'very important lady' less HER, rearranged, gives these letters, and searches found no source or blog for the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Journalist gets very important lady upset, having left her

clue.text: Gangster, one held in confidence as a selfless individual

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

indicators.note: held in means the numeral sits inside the word for confidence

parts.note: trust means confidence or faith
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mobster confides in someone and turns out to be generous.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is Al Capone, the crossword's stock gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: An altruist acts for others' welfare without self-interest.

clue.text: Source of oil in Leeds surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected arrangement, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find oil being produced in Leeds, a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed, the seed of flax, is pressed to make linseed oil.

clue.text: There's very little Irish poetry (just a bit)

parts.note: a little version of very is its abbreviation V
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: There is hardly any Irish poetry, only a fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very little' looks like a quantity, but it means very shortened to V; the bracket tells you the definition is a single piece of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse is one stanza or line of a poem, a small portion of it.

clue.text: River bird is here — originally from a foreign river

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of the word here

explanation.surface: A bird on a river has arrived from a waterway abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: Rhenish means of the Rhine, a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish describes things belonging to the Rhine and its region, such as its wine.

clue.text: Hit leads to a duck? Jolly good!

parts.note: a whack is a heavy blow, a hit
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, written as O

explanation.surface: A cricketer's big swing ends in getting out for nothing, and someone cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a duck, zero, hence O. Whacko is dated British slang for an exclamation of delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacko is an old-fashioned exclamation of delight, like splendid.

clue.text: Shamefaced, giving cruel advice on how to get rid of wicked setter?

definitions.text: cruel advice on how to get rid of wicked setter?

explanation.surface: A sheepish look accompanies brutal instructions for dealing with a nasty dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter is a gun dog breed, not a puzzle setter: the second reading is the order to hang the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangdog means guilty and abashed in appearance, and read as two words it tells someone to execute the dog.

clue.text: Funny liberal member of the upper house gets up

indicators.note: gets up means the whole sequence is turned upwards, read from the bottom in this down entry

parts.note: a lord sits in the House of Lords, the upper house of Parliament

explanation.surface: An amusing peer from the Liberal benches rises to his feet in the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'gets up' turns the letters to read bottom to top: L LORD becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry, whimsical way.

clue.text: That angel outside has eaten that fruit

indicators.note: has eaten means the words before it hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: An angel standing outside has devoured a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts at the last letter of 'That' and ends at the first of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed when delving into company's statement of principles

indicators.note: delving into means the colour word goes inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
someone embarrassed looks red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone blushes while digging into a firm's mission statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a set of beliefs that guide someone.

clue.text: One whose profession is 12

parts.note: 12 across means listening intently, but read literally it describes a specialist whose job is all about hearing organs

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 12 across, read literally as a medical specialty rather than as attentiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist is a doctor who studies and treats disorders of the ear.

clue.text: An ex accounting for why one got one's fingers burnt?

definitions.text: accounting for why one got one's fingers burnt?

explanation.surface: A former partner explains why someone got hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: an aged fire would scorch the fingers, while 'burnt fingers' also means hurt by a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, and literally an ancient fire could burn the hand.

clue.text: Naughty Percy has locked up Henry? It's nothing!

indicators.note: has locked up means the jumbled name holds the other letter inside it
naughty means badly behaved, so the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Badly behaved Percy has imprisoned Henry, and shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' turns PERCY into CYPER, and 'has locked up' puts H inside it. The henry is the SI unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypher, or cipher, is a zero, a figure of no value.
